newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler to forego sick-pay cuts for time.
newsitem.headline: Daimler to forego sick-pay cuts for time.

text.p: German industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG, the first German company to attempt to adopt a new law cutting workers' sick-pay, on Wednesday said it plans to forego cuts until an industry agreement is reached.

German companies and workers have been locked in a bitter debate on the whether old wage contracts will permit companies to implement a new law letting them reduce a worker's pay to 80 percent during illness.
The new law became effective on October 1 and immediately unleashed a wave of protests with workers staging brief strikes at various companies including Daimler-Benz plants.
Daimler on Wednesday said it would now hold off implementing the new law until it had reached a "contractual clarification" on the issue with the union.
The IG Metall union has said that implementing the new law while the old wage contracts were still in effect was illegal.
The union and metal industry employers had met for talks including the sick pay dispute earlier this week, but they broke down early Wednesday with no agreement reached on the issue.
